title: Scriptures are God-breathed (IV.1)
english: Book IV opens: for matters this great, common notions are not enough; we take as proof the testimonies of the writings believed divine — old covenant and new — [[God-breathed Scripture >> Bible:2 Timothy 3:16]].
translator_notes: Copy-text Koetschau GCS 22 (1913) Rufinus Latin; disclose Rufinus paraphrase.
True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B; no ANF Crombie / Butterworth.
Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
Greek Philocalia overlap for IV.1–3 noted; tip follows Rufinus running Latin.

title: How to read: stumbling at the letter; examples (IV.2–3)
english: Many err by not reading spiritually and by forcing the letter where it is impossible or unworthy. Yet history is not to be thrown away wherever the letter keeps its coherence; spiritual sense and letter can stand together. Examples from the law and the Gospels train the reader.
translator_notes: Copy-text Koetschau GCS 22 (1913) Rufinus Latin; disclose Rufinus paraphrase.
True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B; no ANF Crombie / Butterworth.
Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Recap of Father, Son, Spirit — BOOK IV CLOSEOUT SERIES CLOSEOUT
english: A closing recapitulation gathers what was said of Father, Son, and Holy Spirit and the other heads of the church’s preaching, so the reader holds the rule before further inquiry. BOOK IV CLOSEOUT. SERIES CLOSEOUT.
